brief: #103 gave the plaza's paving a moss CA and it works, but moss[] is deliberately plaza-only: it runs on 730 PATH cells and pavingAt's other five kinds are untouched, so the quay, the towpath, the lane and the cross street do not age at all. The town's oldest-looking surface is its newest one. Extend the ageing to at least the quay strip against the rail, which needs no new machinery — a second region in stepMoss, the same creep off the four-neighbour mean, the same scuffing by feet. Judge it at the shipping size: a difference image and a number, not two screenshots.
successLooksLike: By late autumn the quay's joints against the rail are visibly greener than the line people walk, and the plaza's own moss is unchanged from HEAD.
avoid: Do not widen the region by relaxing pavingAt's test — a threshold on a REGION is an intersection, so sample how much of the quay strip the consumer's set actually covers before believing a number. And the skip guard is the trap here: `!shelter && !value` means 'not my cell' only until the value first reaches zero, after which the cell is dead forever.
